title: Introduce scoped service profiles, KMS claim mirroring, and audit hinting
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add new RBAC service profile resource and KMS claim mirroring; audit hinting improves downstream retention and log tagging. No public API changes expected for consumers.
description: Summary: This PR introduces 'scoped service profiles' (an RBAC v2 primitive for binding service-level policies to operator/service roles with an explicit location marker), a KMS claim mirroring shim to attach stable residency metadata to wrapped keys, and an 'audit hinting' mechanism that surfaces high-confidence residency and consent signals into audit events so downstream retention and scrubbing pipelines can make better decisions. Motivation: customers requested stronger guarantees for service-scoped role separation and deterministic KMS residency metadata (see SUP-712). Previous approaches relied on ad-hoc headers and per-call heuristics; this PR formalizes the contract and emits metadata that is verifiable by the audit pipeline. Design highlights: 1) ServiceProfile CRD equivalent in the platform config (pkg/auth/service_profile.go) describing allowed regions, allowed kms_providers, and temporal scope. 2) Runtime enforcement hook (pkg/auth/enforcer.go) that validates incoming operator tokens against the profile and rejects cross-zone binds unless explicitly allowed. 3) KMS claim mirroring (pkg/kms/claim_mirror.go) which, after key wrapping, mirrors the resolver-determined residency claim into a signed claim blob attached to the key metadata (and also emits a compact proof into the audit envelope). The design intentionally avoids changing customer-supplied CMK identifiers — it augments metadata only. 4) Audit hinting (internal/audit/hinting.go) tags events with a small set of normalized hints (residency=eu-west-1, consent=opted-in, profile_id=svc-payments) to drive downstream retention/scrubbing and to improve telemetry cardinality. Backwards compatibility: all new fields are optional; systems that don't understand the hints will ignore them. Migration: a lightweight migration migrates existing per-tenant region overrides into service profiles for services that opt-in (see migration plan in docs/migrations/README). Security considerations: signing of mirrored claims uses existing KMS signing flow and is validated by the audit forwarder. The mirror shim includes a TTL to prevent stale assertions. Testing: unit tests for enforcement logic, integration tests for claim mirroring with a local KMS stub, and an e2e scenario exercising audit hint propagation into the retention pipeline. Related: ENG-2491 defines the service-profile schema and rollout guidance. Files changed (high level): - pkg/auth/service_profile.go (new): schema and validation helpers - pkg/auth/enforcer.go (mod): hook to check service profile before RBAC evaluation - pkg/kms/claim_mirror.go (new): mirror + sign claim blobs - internal/audit/hinting.go (new): canonical hint mapping + legacy compatibility - cmd/installer/migrations/service_profiles_migrate.go (new): opt-in migration driver - docs/migrations/README.md (mod): migration steps + operator checklist - tests/integration/kms_claim_mirror_test.go (new) - go.mod, go.sum (deps: added github.com/sigsum/compactproof v0.1.2) Commits: ["39f2d8b: add service profile schema and basic validation", "a4b7e9c: enforcement hook and policy check unit tests", "d12f6a3: initial claim mirroring implementation and signing flow", "c3e0b11: add audit hinting mapper and unit tests", "e5f4a90: add migration driver and migration docs", "f999c2a: integration tests for claim mirroring (kms stub)"] Review conversation (high level): - Diego Ramirez (reviewer) — "This looks like a solid approach to avoiding header-based heuristics. A couple of asks: make the profile validation deterministic when region lists are unordered and add a small benchmark for the enforcer hook under 5000 rps." — Author reply: "Agree on deterministic validation; normalized sorting added. I'll add a micro-benchmark and include numbers in follow-up." - Aisha Kapoor (security) — "Please ensure mirrored claims cannot be replayed across keys; add a nonce or bind to key-id." — Author reply: "Claim now includes key_id binding and a short nonce; TTL enforced by mirror middleware." - Noah Patel (sre) — "CI failed initially on the newly added dependency; why was compactproof chosen over existing libs?" — Author reply: "Compactproof provides the succinct proof shape we need with minimal allocations. Added fallback helpers and pinned version to avoid surprises." - Diego (follow-up) — "One minor nit: error messages from enforcer leak internal tenant ids in logs when validation fails. Can we scrub or replace with stable hashes?" — Author reply: "Good catch — replaced direct ids with HMAC-derived fingerprints using the existing audit-key; tests updated." CI checks: - lint: pass - unit tests: pass - integration-tests/kms-stub: fail (flaky network during first run) — rerun — pass - build: pass Merge: squash and merge. Merge commit message: "Introduce scoped service profiles, KMS claim mirroring, and audit hinting — Maya Chen" Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag feature.service_profiles.enabled. Phase 1: server-side validation only (2 weeks). Phase 2: enable mirrored claim emission for services in beta cohort (4 weeks). Phase 3: enable hinting in audit forwarder and update retention rules (after verification). Notes for operators: - To opt a service into a service profile, add a profile.yaml following docs/migrations/README.md and run cmd/installer migrate-service-profiles --service svc-name. - Mirrored claims are signed and appended to key metadata under key.metadata["residency_claim"]. The value is compactproof base64; audit forwarder will copy a redacted hint into the log. Post-merge follow-ups (tracked as separate linear tickets): - Add micro-benchmark for enforcer (ENG-2510) - Enable automatic profile discovery from service manifests (ENG-2511) - Dashboard for mirrored-claim telemetry in Console (PM-78)
